gen-dafont-alien-encounters-gf-ovo: Ovo keeps its thins barely lighter than its thicks, with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders. And across a full page, soft heavier accents give the reading a gentle pulse, far from Alien Encounters' otherworldly gaps.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-epunda-slab: Commanding, wide and untilted: Amadeus sprawls across the line. Its pipe-like strokes are built for sheer presence, while Epunda Slab, a dignified serif with a gaping c and tall rounded lowercase, is built for reading.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-scope-one: Traditional meets bold: Amadeus, drawn with a constant-width pen line. What lingers is the spill of Scope One's counters into surrounding space, held in check by stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lisu-bosa: Capitals barely rise above lowercase in Azonix, whose ruler-drawn line never changes width. Lisu Bosa's tall, sturdy lowercase and lightly flexed spring-wire contrast give the rigid heading its single best foil.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-domine: Dignified Domine takes over after the big round lowercase bowls of Bloody. Domine's unhurried ebb and flow of stroke thickness, plus a breathing space inside every curved glyph, is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-esteban: Big round bowls, loud attitude: Bloody leads, and Esteban's lowercase looks oversized beside its own capitals. And the heading earns its keep when big and short, leaving Esteban's quiet stroke contrast to carry the rest.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-halant: Bloody brings big round lowercase bowls and a commanding swagger, then hands the line over to quieter type. Halant's towering x-height and faint thick-thin shift carry on from there.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-headland-one: Headland One keeps its letters well apart, with a tall rounded o. Beneath the big round bowls of Bloody, gentle stroke variation and generous spacing give everything a dignified, traditional footing.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hedvig-letters-seri: Loud round bowls, then a steady voice: Bloody meets Hedvig Letters Serif. Its open-ended curves and sturdy tall lowercase carry a faint nib-pressure variation, so next to the round-bowled heading it feels authoritative and unhurried.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lisu-bosa: Bloody comes in with big round lowercase bowls and a commanding stance. Where that heading dominates, Lisu Bosa reads: sturdy tall lowercase, counters that spill into surrounding space, and a lightly flexed spring-wire contrast.
